paragraphs: Here's what I want you to hold onto, friend. Jesus speaks, and everything He speaks to listens. A demon, a fever, a whole line of sick people at sunset: none of it gets to stay when He gives the word. The people in the synagogue said it themselves: "With authority and power He commands the unclean spirits, and they come out!" (Luke 4:36). That's who is standing in front of you every time you open this book.

Now look at what that authority was doing. He laid His hands on each one and healed them (Luke 4:40). Not a crowd-control wave from across the room. Each. One. And He stood over one woman with a fever in one house, and she got up and served. I've been forgotten in the back of a drawer, so I know how good it feels to be seen up close by Someone with that kind of power. He is never too big to notice you.

But the crowds wanted to keep Him right there, and He said no. "I must preach the good news of the kingdom of God to the other towns as well, because that is why I was sent" (Luke 4:43). Healing was a gift, and the good news was the mission. So the question for you, baker, is simple: what are you listening to Him for? Come for the help, stay for the good news, and then pass it on, because the good news keeps MOVING and the story isn't over.
